findings.issue_text: Date-override semantics inverted for 'unavailable all day' overrides: uses === on two distinct dayjs object instances (always false) so a zero-length day-off override can never be detected, and the surrounding logic makes every slot on an override day available instead of unavailable
Working-hours check uses slot start time as both start and end (end is identical to start, ignoring eventLength), so slots that overrun working hours pass the check
Working-hours/UTC-offset comparison against wrong timezone: slotStartTime is forced to UTC so hour()/minute() are UTC wall-clock values but workingHour.startTime/endTime are organizer-local minutes

Adding utcOffset to an absolute instant with .add() shifts the instant instead of converting its representation; should use .tz(organizerTimeZone) so boundary slots aren't misclassified by the offset amount

Override offset math in packages/lib/slots.ts can produce out-of-range/negative minute values or midnight wrap (startTime > endTime), causing the working-hour unset loop to match the wrong range and leave double-bookable times
organizerTimeZone may be undefined (userSchedule?.timeZone), silently defaulting utcOffset to 0 so date-override day matching is done against UTC instead of the organizer's zone

Duplicate/parallel availability logic in packages/lib/slots.ts and checkIfIsAvailable uses different offset math that will diverge on DST-transition days, producing inconsistent slot lists between generation and filtering

Reference-equality comparison of two distinct dayjs objects in checkIfIsAvailable (~line 108, slots.ts) is always false, making the zero-length override branch dead and forcing the full override-scan cost per slot; should use .isSame()

Per-slot repeated dayjs allocations and .format('YYYY MM DD') string allocations inside the override check in checkIfIsAvailable; utcOffset and shifted date.start/date.end should be precomputed once per override outside the slot loop
O(slots × users²) userAvailability.find() lookup inside per-slot/per-user filtering in slots.ts (~line 579); should be a precomputed Map<userId, timeZone>

Redundant working-hours filtering per slot in checkIfIsAvailable (~lines 137–152) duplicating constraints already applied during slot generation; also `end` is computed from slotStartTime rather than the slot end time
Repeated dayjs(override.start.toString()) string-parse round-trip per override in lib/slots.ts (~line 211) instead of dayjs(override.start).tz(...)

In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts (~line 140), object identity comparison `===` on two dayjs objects is always false; should use `.isSame(...)`, making the zero-length override branch dead code

In the same file (~line 158), `end` is computed from the same expression as `start` (both from slot start time), so the working-hours check never verifies slot end against working-hour end, letting long-duration slots pass outside working hours

In the same file, `dateOverrideExist` returns true before the `busy.every(...)` check, so slots inside a date override are returned as available without checking the host's bookings, risking overbooking
In the same file, wrong timezone passed as `organizerTimeZone` (`schedule.timeZone` is the invitee's timezone, not the organizer's), producing wrong override-day matching when timezones differ

In the same file, working-hours check uses UTC wall-clock hours and UTC day-of-week against working hours stored in local time, making the check wrong for non-UTC hosts; also duplicates filtering already done in `getAvailableSlots`

In the same file, `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)` misused (Date object ignores parsing semantics) and `utcOffset() * -1` inverts the sign, so the offset shifts in the wrong direction for most zones

In packages/lib/slots.ts (~line 210), offset shift on override minutes can roll over across midnight, zeroing working hours for the wrong day and allowing startTime to exceed endTime; also uses offset at override.start's instant which is wrong under DST

In packages/lib/slots.ts, `dayjs(override.start.toString())` parses a Date via locale-dependent toString() which is fragile, and breaks if `override.timeZone` is unset (typed optional), making `dayjs().tz(undefined)` throw or default unpredictably

In the slots.ts viewer router, `userSchedule?.timeZone` may be undefined when `userAvailability.find(...)` misses, and the `organizerTimeZone ? ... : 0` fallback silently treats the override as UTC, masking data inconsistencies

checkIfIsAvailable working-hours filter has a bug: slot end time is computed using the slot's start time (slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute() used twice), so slots extending past workingHour.endTime incorrectly pass the check; no test covers this branch
No test coverage for the new working-hours filter in checkIfIsAvailable (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts ~130-145)
dayjs(date.start) === dayjs(date.end) reference-equality comparison is always false, making the zero-length override path dead code (slots.ts:113)

No tests for slots on an override day but outside the override window; behavior change excluding such slots even within regular working hours is validated only by a single happy-path test (slots.ts:102-127)

New timezone test (getSchedule.test.ts:787-803) lacks a negative control and a negative UTC offset case, where YYYY MM DD day-matching can misclassify; inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset arithmetic in packages/lib/slots.ts:213 is untested
packages/lib/slots.ts override-offset rewrite (lines 211-222) has no tests for overrides crossing UTC midnight, DST transition days, or same-timezone (offset 0) regression behavior

Organizer timezone fallback chain (slots.ts:439-440: eventType.timeZone → schedule.timeZone → userAvailability[0]?.timeZone) untested, including undefined-timezone fallback silently using utcOffset = 0 and multi-host events with differing host timezones

Slots inside a date override bypass all busy/booking checks: dateOverrides.find only returns truthy for slots outside the override window, so slots inside the override fall through to 'if (dateOverrideExist) return true' without evaluating busy checks, allowing double-bookings
`===` comparison on Dayjs objects in the override find callback is always false since it compares object references, making the 'start == end' branch dead code; should use .isSame() or valueOf()
Copy-paste bug in working-hours block: 'end' is computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so the end check never considers eventLength and slots can overhang past working hours
Days with no working hours (e.g. Sunday with no workingHours entry) are treated as fully available since workingHours.find returns undefined, skipping the 'outside working hours' early return

UTC-offset sign inversion in organizer-day computation: negating utcOffset() moves the timestamp west instead of to organizer local time, causing override day-matching to fail near midnight; also organizerTimeZone being optional silently degrades to offset 0

Cross-midnight/DST breaks in override minute computation: overrides like 23:00–01:00 wrap around producing startTime > endTime, and the offset computed from override.start applied to end is wrong across DST transitions
override.timeZone may be undefined at other getSlots call sites since TimeRange.timeZone was made optional, causing dayjs(...).tz(undefined) to throw at request time
New test uses a fixed non-DST timezone and asserts the same UTC slots, so it cannot catch DST-offset bugs, sign errors, or the dead === branch — it's near-tautological

adjudication_records.issue_text: Date-override semantics inverted for 'unavailable all day' overrides: uses === on two distinct dayjs object instances (always false) so a zero-length day-off override can never be detected, and the surrounding logic makes every slot on an override day available instead of unavailable
Working-hours check uses slot start time as both start and end (end is identical to start, ignoring eventLength), so slots that overrun working hours pass the check
Working-hours/UTC-offset comparison against wrong timezone: slotStartTime is forced to UTC so hour()/minute() are UTC wall-clock values but workingHour.startTime/endTime are organizer-local minutes

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours gate computes `slotStartTime = time.utc()` and then derives `start`/`end` minutes from `slotStartTime.hour()/minute()` and `slotStartTime.day()`. It compares those UTC wall-clock values to `workingHour.startTime/endTime` and `workingHour.days` (which represent working-hours minutes/day-of-week in the schedule’s local context). The diff shows no conversion using `organizerTimeZone` (passed in) or any other timezone when checking working hours, so for non-UTC timezones this can reject/accept slots incorrectly due to timezone/day boundary shifts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding utcOffset to an absolute instant with .add() shifts the instant instead of converting its representation; should use .tz(organizerTimeZone) so boundary slots aren't misclassified by the offset amount

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the date-override boundaries are adjusted via `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` where `utcOffset` is derived from `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`. Using `.add()` changes the underlying instant, not just its timezone representation, so comparisons like `slotEndTime.isBefore(dayjs(date.start).add(...))` and the `YYYY MM DD` day-matching can be shifted by the offset amount, potentially misclassifying slots around day boundaries. This aligns with the finding that `.tz(organizerTimeZone)` (representation conversion) should be used instead of offset-adding (instant shifting). Similar instant-shifting logic also exists in `packages/lib/slots.ts` for overrides (`dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Override offset math in packages/lib/slots.ts can produce out-of-range/negative minute values or midnight wrap (startTime > endTime), causing the working-hour unset loop to match the wrong range and leave double-bookable times

adjudication.rationale: In packages/lib/slots.ts the new override conversion computes `startTime`/`endTime` as `dayjs(...).hour() * 60 + ...minute()`, which always yields a 0–1439 minute-of-day value; it cannot produce negative or out-of-range minutes as claimed. While a start/end “wrap” issue is theoretically possible in some edge cases (e.g., DST changes) the diff does not show the unset loop logic nor any demonstrated case where `startTime > endTime` causes incorrect matching, so the specific defect described is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organizerTimeZone may be undefined (userSchedule?.timeZone), silently defaulting utcOffset to 0 so date-override day matching is done against UTC instead of the organizer's zone

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the date-override day matching computes `utcOffset` as `0` when `organizerTimeZone` is falsy (`const utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? ... : 0;`). In `getSchedule`, at least one call site passes `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone`, which can be `undefined` if `userAvailability.find(...)` fails or the found schedule lacks `timeZone`. In that case, override-day comparison falls back to UTC (`slotStartTime` is `time.utc()`), potentially mis-evaluating whether an override applies for the organizer’s actual timezone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate/parallel availability logic in packages/lib/slots.ts and checkIfIsAvailable uses different offset math that will diverge on DST-transition days, producing inconsistent slot lists between generation and filtering

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows parallel handling of date overrides in two places with different offset calculations: `packages/lib/slots.ts` converts override start/end into minute-of-day using `organizerUtcOffset` vs `inviteeUtcOffset` (offset = invitee - organizer) and then `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")...`, while `checkIfIsAvailable` in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts` applies `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` against `slotStartTime`/`slotEndTime`. This is concretely divergent logic for the same concept (date overrides), which can lead to inconsistent slot generation vs slot filtering, and DST-transition concerns are plausible given the differing offset derivations, though the exact DST failure isn’t directly proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reference-equality comparison of two distinct dayjs objects in checkIfIsAvailable (~line 108, slots.ts) is always false, making the zero-length override branch dead and forcing the full override-scan cost per slot; should use .isSame()
matched_golden_ids: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: comparing two dayjs instances with strict/reference equality (===) will never be true because they are different objects, making that branch effectively dead; the fix is to use dayjs value comparison via .isSame() instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-slot repeated dayjs allocations and .format('YYYY MM DD') string allocations inside the override check in checkIfIsAvailable; utcOffset and shifted date.start/date.end should be precomputed once per override outside the slot loop

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new date override logic repeatedly constructs `dayjs` objects and does `.format("YYYY MM DD")` inside `dateOverrides.find(...)` (e.g., multiple `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,"minutes")` / `dayjs(date.end)...` calls) and also recomputes `utcOffset` per override. Since `checkIfIsAvailable` is invoked per slot in the schedule loop, this creates per-slot repeated allocations/work that could be precomputed once per override (shifted start/end and day key) outside the slot loop. This is a performance/efficiency concern, not a correctness defect evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: O(slots × users²) userAvailability.find() lookup inside per-slot/per-user filtering in slots.ts (~line 579); should be a precomputed Map<userId, timeZone>

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a per-slot/per-user lookup: `const userSchedule = userAvailability.find(({ user: { id: userId } }) => userId === slotUserId);` inside `slot.userIds?.filter(...)`. Since this runs for each slot and each userId in the slot, and `find` is linear in `userAvailability`, it can create avoidable O(slots × users × userAvailability) overhead (often ~O(slots × users²)). Precomputing a `Map<userId, timeZone>` would remove the repeated linear search. This is a performance/scalability concern, not a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redundant working-hours filtering per slot in checkIfIsAvailable (~lines 137–152) duplicating constraints already applied during slot generation; also `end` is computed from slotStartTime rather than the slot end time
Repeated dayjs(override.start.toString()) string-parse round-trip per override in lib/slots.ts (~line 211) instead of dayjs(override.start).tz(...)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new logic computes offsets via `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(...)` (and similarly for invitee). This introduces an unnecessary Date->string->parse round-trip per override and repeats parsing work. The diff shows this can be replaced with `dayjs(override.start).tz(...)` to avoid extra parsing/overhead and reduce reliance on string parsing behavior; however, the diff alone doesn’t prove it causes incorrect behavior in practice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts (~line 140), object identity comparison `===` on two dayjs objects is always false; should use `.isSame(...)`, making the zero-length override branch dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the new date override logic compares two freshly-created Dayjs instances with `===`: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))`. Since these are distinct objects, the identity comparison will always be false, so the intended “zero-length override” branch is effectively dead and will never trigger. This should use a value comparison such as `.isSame(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the same file (~line 158), `end` is computed from the same expression as `start` (both from slot start time), so the working-hours check never verifies slot end against working-hour end, letting long-duration slots pass outside working hours

In the same file, `dateOverrideExist` returns true before the `busy.every(...)` check, so slots inside a date override are returned as available without checking the host's bookings, risking overbooking

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, after the new date-override logic, the function does `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` before reaching the final `return busy.every((busyTime) => { ... })` block. Since `dateOverrideExist` is set to true when a date override exists for the slot’s day, slots deemed “within the date override” will be returned as available without evaluating `busy` conflicts (host bookings), matching the finding’s overbooking risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the same file, wrong timezone passed as `organizerTimeZone` (`schedule.timeZone` is the invitee's timezone, not the organizer's), producing wrong override-day matching when timezones differ

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the override-day matching relies on `organizerTimeZone` to compute an offset (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`). But in `getSchedule`, the first availability check now passes `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` (and similarly `userSchedule.timeZone` elsewhere) even though an `organizerTimeZone` is computed earlier from `eventType`/`userAvailability`. If `schedule.timeZone` is the invitee/request timezone (as the finding claims), this would miscompute the offset and cause wrong date-override day matching when organizer/invitee timezones differ. The diff shows this potentially incorrect wiring (`organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone`) and the logic is timezone-sensitive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the same file, working-hours check uses UTC wall-clock hours and UTC day-of-week against working hours stored in local time, making the check wrong for non-UTC hosts; also duplicates filtering already done in `getAvailableSlots`

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours gate uses `slotStartTime = time.utc()` and then checks `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())` plus `slotStartTime.hour()/minute()` against `workingHour.startTime/endTime` (which are typically defined in the organizer’s local schedule time). The passed `organizerTimeZone` is not applied in this working-hours check, so for non-UTC organizers the day-of-week and minutes-of-day can be wrong. Additionally, it computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, making the bounds check incorrect even in UTC (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`). This is a concrete, diff-introduced correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the same file, `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)` misused (Date object ignores parsing semantics) and `utcOffset() * -1` inverts the sign, so the offset shifts in the wrong direction for most zones

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and then `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`. From the code alone, the claim that `dayjs.tz()` is “misused” with a `Date` isn’t verifiable (Dayjs timezone APIs accept `Date` values, and offset lookup still works). Also, multiplying `utcOffset()` by `-1` is not inherently “wrong direction”: if the intent is to convert a wall-clock time in `organizerTimeZone` into a UTC-shifted instant, using `-utcOffset` and adding it is a standard way to do that for both positive and negative offsets. Whether the overall adjustment is needed depends on how `date.start/end` are stored/defined, which is not established by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/lib/slots.ts (~line 210), offset shift on override minutes can roll over across midnight, zeroing working hours for the wrong day and allowing startTime to exceed endTime; also uses offset at override.start's instant which is wrong under DST

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new override conversion computes `offset` once using `override.start` (`organizerUtcOffset`/`inviteeUtcOffset`), then applies it to both `override.start` and `override.end` and finally derives minutes-of-day via `.hour()*60 + .minute()`. This discards the date component, so if the offset shift pushes a time across midnight, the resulting `startTime`/`endTime` can wrap and become inconsistent (including `startTime > endTime`), causing the subsequent “unset working hours” loop to target the wrong day’s minutes. Also, using the offset at the start instant for the end time is incorrect when a DST transition occurs between `start` and `end` (offset can differ at `override.end`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In packages/lib/slots.ts, `dayjs(override.start.toString())` parses a Date via locale-dependent toString() which is fragile, and breaks if `override.timeZone` is unset (typed optional), making `dayjs().tz(undefined)` throw or default unpredictably

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `packages/lib/slots.ts` now does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` (and similarly for `timeZone`). This is a real review issue: (1) parsing via `Date#toString()` is unnecessary/fragile compared to passing the `Date` directly (`dayjs(override.start)`), and (2) `override.timeZone` is not guarded even though the type added in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts` makes `timeZone?: string` optional, so this code relies on `dayjs.tz` behavior with `undefined` (likely falling back to local/default timezone), which can produce incorrect offsets. However, from the diff alone it’s not provable that this will definitely throw at runtime or that `override.timeZone` is ever actually unset, since `getSchedule` now populates `timeZone: availability.timeZone` when flattening overrides.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the slots.ts viewer router, `userSchedule?.timeZone` may be undefined when `userAvailability.find(...)` misses, and the `organizerTimeZone ? ... : 0` fallback silently treats the override as UTC, masking data inconsistencies

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, date-override handling computes `utcOffset` as `organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0`. The diff shows callers can pass `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` (where `userSchedule` comes from `userAvailability.find(...)`), so `organizerTimeZone` can be `undefined`. In that case the code silently uses `0` (UTC) when comparing override dates/times (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, ...)` vs `slotStartTime`), which can yield incorrect availability decisions for non-UTC organizers and does hide the underlying mismatch/missing timezone data instead of falling back to the previously computed organizer timezone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: checkIfIsAvailable working-hours filter has a bug: slot end time is computed using the slot's start time (slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute() used twice), so slots extending past workingHour.endTime incorrectly pass the check; no test covers this branch
matched_golden_ids: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same bug: the slot end time is incorrectly calculated using slotStartTime (start time used twice) instead of using slotEndTime, causing availability checks against workingHour.endTime to be wrong.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for the new working-hours filter in checkIfIsAvailable (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts ~130-145)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial working-hours gating logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` (the `workingHours.find(...)` block that returns `false` when a slot is outside `workingHour.startTime/endTime`), but the only added test in `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts` covers a date-override timezone scenario and does not exercise the new working-hours filter branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: dayjs(date.start) === dayjs(date.end) reference-equality comparison is always false, making the zero-length override path dead code (slots.ts:113)

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), the code compares `dayjs(date.start).add(... ) === dayjs(date.end).add(... )`. This uses `===` on two newly-created Dayjs objects, which will be reference-unequal even if they represent the same instant, so the “zero-length override” branch is effectively dead/unreachable as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests for slots on an override day but outside the override window; behavior change excluding such slots even within regular working hours is validated only by a single happy-path test (slots.ts:102-127)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial availability logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` to treat a day with any matching `dateOverrides` as a special case: if an override exists for the slot’s date and the slot is outside the override window, it returns `false` (early return in the new override block around `dateOverrides.find(...)` / `return false`; otherwise `dateOverrideExist` causes `return true` and skips working-hours checks). The only test added in this PR (`getSchedule.test.ts`) asserts a happy-path timezone alignment for override-day slots, but the diff does not add a test exercising the new exclusion behavior for slots on an override day that fall outside the override window (while potentially within `workingHours`). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-coverage concern for the new branching behavior, not a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New timezone test (getSchedule.test.ts:787-803) lacks a negative control and a negative UTC offset case, where YYYY MM DD day-matching can misclassify; inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset arithmetic in packages/lib/slots.ts:213 is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial timezone-offset arithmetic for date overrides in `packages/lib/slots.ts` (computing `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` and shifting override start/end by that offset), but the only new test added in `getSchedule.test.ts` exercises a single positive invitee timezone (`Timezones["+6:00"]`) and asserts the same UTC slot outputs. There is no corresponding test covering negative offsets or day-boundary scenarios that could validate the new offset-difference logic across different organizer/invitee offsets. This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts override-offset rewrite (lines 211-222) has no tests for overrides crossing UTC midnight, DST transition days, or same-timezone (offset 0) regression behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites override time calculations in `packages/lib/slots.ts` to adjust by the difference between organizer and invitee UTC offsets (using `dayjs(...).tz(...).utcOffset()` and `add(offset, "minute")`). While `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts` adds one test for a date override in a different timezone, the diff does not show any tests specifically covering (a) overrides that cross UTC midnight after applying the offset, (b) DST transition days where `utcOffset()` changes, or (c) same-timezone behavior where `offset` should be 0. Given the nontrivial new offset logic, these are concrete missing edge-case tests grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer timezone fallback chain (slots.ts:439-440: eventType.timeZone → schedule.timeZone → userAvailability[0]?.timeZone) untested, including undefined-timezone fallback silently using utcOffset = 0 and multi-host events with differing host timezones

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/expands timezone-sensitive logic that depends on `organizerTimeZone` being correct, but the tests added only cover a date-override scenario with a different *invitee* timezone, not the organizer-timezone fallback chain or undefined organizer timezone. In `checkIfIsAvailable`, date override comparisons use `organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 : 0`, so an undefined `organizerTimeZone` silently falls back to offset `0` (UTC) and could change behavior without coverage. Additionally, while `getSchedule` now sometimes passes per-user timezones (`organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` / `userSchedule?.timeZone`) for multi-host cases, there is no diff evidence of tests validating multi-host events where hosts have differing timezones and how the fallback (`eventType.timeZone || eventType?.schedule?.timeZone || userAvailability?.[0]?.timeZone`) behaves.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Slots inside a date override bypass all busy/booking checks: dateOverrides.find only returns truthy for slots outside the override window, so slots inside the override fall through to 'if (dateOverrideExist) return true' without evaluating busy checks, allowing double-bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new date-override block can return `true` before the final `busy.every(...)` evaluation. Specifically, when a matching-date override exists and the slot is within the override window, `dateOverrideExist` is set to `true`, `dateOverrides.find(...)` returns falsy (because the callback only `return true` for slots outside the override), and then `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` executes. This bypasses the subsequent busy/booking overlap checks (`return busy.every(...)`), allowing a slot to be marked available even if it overlaps `busy` times (double-booking).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `===` comparison on Dayjs objects in the override find callback is always false since it compares object references, making the 'start == end' branch dead code; should use .isSame() or valueOf()

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, inside the `dateOverrides.find` callback, the code does `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))`. These expressions create new Dayjs objects, so `===` compares object identity and will always be false unless they are the same instance, making that branch effectively dead. This is a correctness issue in the newly added override logic; it should use `.isSame(...)` or compare timestamps (e.g., `.valueOf()`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy-paste bug in working-hours block: 'end' is computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so the end check never considers eventLength and slots can overhang past working hours
Days with no working hours (e.g. Sunday with no workingHours entry) are treated as fully available since workingHours.find returns undefined, skipping the 'outside working hours' early return

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours guard only returns `false` when `workingHours.find(...)` finds an entry for the slot’s weekday *and* the slot is outside that entry’s range. If there is no `WorkingHours` entry whose `days` includes `slotStartTime.day()`, the callback never returns `true`, `find` returns `undefined`, and the function does not early-return `false`, falling through to the `busy.every(...)` check. That makes days with no working-hours entry effectively unrestricted by working hours, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UTC-offset sign inversion in organizer-day computation: negating utcOffset() moves the timestamp west instead of to organizer local time, causing override day-matching to fail near midnight; also organizerTimeZone being optional silently degrades to offset 0

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, override-day matching shifts `date.start`/`date.end` by `utcOffset * -1` (e.g. `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` where `utcOffset` is already negated). Since `date.start`/`date.end` are `Date` instants, applying an extra offset can move the instant in the wrong direction and change the UTC day used in `format("YYYY MM DD")`, plausibly breaking matches near midnight. Also, when `organizerTimeZone` is undefined the code falls back to `utcOffset = 0`, which silently changes the day-matching semantics and can incorrectly accept/reject overrides.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cross-midnight/DST breaks in override minute computation: overrides like 23:00–01:00 wrap around producing startTime > endTime, and the offset computed from override.start applied to end is wrong across DST transitions

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, override minutes are computed as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, 'minute').hour()*60 + minute` and similarly for `override.end`, which discards the date component. If an override spans midnight (e.g., 23:00–01:00 next day), this will produce `startTime > endTime` with no handling shown. Additionally, `offset` is derived only from `override.start` (`organizerUtcOffset`/`inviteeUtcOffset` based on start) and then applied to both start and end; across a DST transition between start and end, the correct offset may differ at `override.end`, making `endTime` wrong. The diff contains no adjustment for these cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: override.timeZone may be undefined at other getSlots call sites since TimeRange.timeZone was made optional, causing dayjs(...).tz(undefined) to throw at request time

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new logic calls `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` to compute offsets, but `TimeRange.timeZone` was changed to optional (`timeZone?: string`) in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts` and there is no fallback/guard when `override.timeZone` is missing. The diff shows `getSchedule` now populates `timeZone` when flattening `dateOverrides`, but it does not prove all `getSlots` call sites (or all `activeOverrides` sources) will always include it, so this is a concrete robustness/edge-case issue rather than a fully verifiable crash from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New test uses a fixed non-DST timezone and asserts the same UTC slots, so it cannot catch DST-offset bugs, sign errors, or the dead === branch — it's near-tautological

adjudication.rationale: The added test calls `getSchedule` with `timeZone: Timezones["+6:00"]` (a fixed-offset, non-DST zone) and explicitly comments/assumes “it should return the same as this is the utc time”, then asserts a fixed set of UTC slot strings. That makes the test largely self-fulfilling for UTC-normalized behavior and does not exercise DST transitions or validate sign/offset-direction correctness in the newly introduced offset logic. This is a concrete test-coverage limitation tied to the specific new test in the diff, not a directly verifiable runtime defect by itself.
